share._readme: Cross-language practices, checked against the CPDD guides and syllabuses by text search on 4 Nov 2026. Paraphrased: MOE text is not reproduced. The 'try' lines are department suggestions, not CPDD advice.
share.lead: All three languages share one syllabus framework, but CPDD built each package differently. Some strong practices sit in one language's guides and have not reached the other two. This page sets out what each language could borrow.

items.name: STAR inquiry activity
items.line: Scenario Analysis, Team Inquiry, Application, Reflection.
items.what: Students unpack a real situation, investigate it in teams, apply what they found, then reflect. It gives teachers a short inquiry they can run inside a normal unit. See How STAR works on the Compare languages page.
items.where: Listed in the ML syllabus (Appendix E, under Singapore Teaching Practice). Used in the ML guides for G2 1B Unit 7, G3 1B Unit 7 (the guide's appendix for Units 5 to 8 also prints the steps), G3 2B Unit 5 and G3 Sec 3 Unit 1. G3 Sec 3 Unit 1 (pp. 24 to 26) is the fullest model, with all four stages written out.
items.gap: It appears in no CL or TL guide or syllabus. It has also not spread within ML: the text search found it in neither the G1 nor the HML guides.
items.why: The ML syllabus files it under Singapore Teaching Practice, which applies to all three languages, so it is not specific to Malay.
items.try: CL: G3 Sec 3 Unit 3, Into the community. TL: G3 2B Unit 3, Youth and society.

ML.t: Syllabus and 4 lesson plans, G2 and G3 only

items.name: Inquiry tasks flagged for weighted assessment
items.line: A teacher note says the task is inquiry and can count as a WA.
items.what: The guide tells teachers outright that a task is inquiry-based, explains what that means for the unit, and says it can serve as a weighted assessment.
items.where: ML G1 Sec 3 Unit 4 and G2 Sec 3 Unit 4, both planning a social business.
items.gap: CL has inquiry-like integrated tasks, but they carry no such label: the department's own reading found 57 across the four courses. No TL guide mentions a weighted assessment, in the text search of the repaired lesson files (5 Nov 2026), and no TL SLS lesson links inquiry to a WA.
items.why: Teachers can see at once which tasks can carry both inquiry and assessment, which saves planning time.
items.try: CL: mark up the 57 integrated tasks already identified on the Sec 1–4 progression page, and agree which could count as a WA.

items.name: 5E inquiry sequence
items.line: Engage, Explore, then onward through the 5E steps, in a group reading task.
items.what: A group works on a text through the named 5E stages instead of answering set comprehension questions.
items.where: TL G3 2B lesson preparation, Units 1 and 2. Separately, an e-pedagogy tag marks inquiry experiences in TL G3 2A Units 2 and 3, and HTL Sec 3 Units 1 and 3 name inquiry learning as the strategy, without the 5E steps.
items.gap: The term 5E does not appear in any CL or ML guide. Within TL it appears only in these two G3 units. The SLS lessons for these units are single media files: the 5E steps are in the guide only.
items.why: It applies inquiry to reading, whereas the ML examples above are mostly discussion or project tasks.
items.try: ML: a reading part in G3 Sec 3. CL: the second reading of a core text in G3 Sec 3.

items.name: 21CC mapped activity by activity
items.line: A column in each unit overview names the competency each activity builds.
items.what: Each TL unit overview has an MOE-initiatives column. Many activity rows name a 21CC domain there, so teachers can see where a competency is meant to be built.
items.where: About 480 of about 1,200 activity rows in the 23 TL Word overviews (G1, G2 and G3 Sec 1 to 4, HTL Sec 1 to 3). The lesson files carry the same tags, and add G3 1A Units 2 to 4 and HTL Sec 4.
items.gap: CL maps one worked example in detail. ML has five teacher notes in G1 Sec 4 Units 1 to 3. So this roadmap's E21CC tags for CL and ML are mostly inferred rather than taken from CPDD. The SLS lessons do not repeat the map. One G2 lesson, a brochure toolkit, prints CCI 5.3, CCI 6.3 and CGC 5.3 with levels.
items.why: E21CC is a 2027 school priority, and a map shows where each competency is taught and where the gaps are.
items.try: ML and CL: add one competency column to one Sec 1 unit plan, using TL's overview format as the model.

items.name: Method for setting a 21CC unit goal
items.line: Choose 2 to 3 competencies a unit can really build, then write one combined goal.
items.what: CL's appendix sets out 21CC goals across four developmental levels, then shows how to choose 2 to 3 that suit a unit and combine them with the language goal.
items.where: The Sec 1A, 1B and Sec 3 CL guides for G1, G2, G3 and HCL (12 guides). The worked example is Sec 1A Unit 3, Meet in the Lion City.
items.gap: ML's guides have no equivalent. TL names competencies with no goal-setting method in its overviews or lesson files. One G3 1B Unit 3 lesson prints a milestone (CCI 1.1c, by Sec 2) with success criteria.
items.why: A tag says a competency is present. A levelled goal says what progress looks like, which is closer to MOE's developmental milestones.
items.try: TL: add a level to the tags in one G3 unit. ML: write one combined goal for a unit that already uses STAR.

TL.t: No method; 1 lesson prints a milestone

items.name: Social-emotional competencies named in activities
items.line: Activities name skills such as self-management, social awareness and responsible decisions.
items.what: TL overviews name the social-emotional competency an activity builds, alongside 21CC, so that it is planned and not left to chance.
items.where: About 200 of about 1,200 activity rows in the TL Word overviews: G2 about 110, HTL about 60, G1 about 20 and G3 under 10. So it has not spread evenly within TL either.
items.gap: In CL guides the words appear only inside the 21CC framework appendix, not against lessons. No ML guide names them.
items.why: Themes such as relationships and well-being already run through all three languages, so the tags fit existing units.
items.try: CL: G3 Sec 3 Unit 1, Friends by your side. ML: G3 Sec 3 Unit 6, One for all, all for one.

items.name: Anecdotal assessment written into lessons
items.line: Lesson plans tell the teacher what to observe and check, and when.
items.what: ML lesson plans prompt quick checks through questioning, discussion or observation, so that teachers can judge readiness before moving to the next part of the unit.
items.where: All 32 ML teacher guides and SOW samples, across every course and year.
items.gap: CL mentions classroom observation in some places, without a named routine in the lesson plan. TL tags some activities as holistic assessment (about 30 overview rows), without saying what to look for. G3 lesson files for Sec 2 to 4 (9 files) add a Know, Understand, Do feedback prompt on what the teacher has noticed in a student.
items.why: It gives every lesson a low-stakes check on learning without adding marking.
items.try: CL: add one observation prompt to each block of one unit. TL: expand the existing holistic assessment tags into look-fors.

items.name: Intended understanding and essential questions
items.line: Each unit starts from what students should understand and what question drives it.
items.what: ML frames units around an intended understanding, and many guides add essential questions (Soalan Penting). The lessons then work toward them.
items.where: Intended understandings appear in 23 ML guides across all four courses. Essential questions are named in 12 ML files.
items.gap: CL sets skill goals and teaches its goal method in the appendix. TL lists learning outcomes per activity. Neither frames units this way in the files read.
items.why: Essential questions are the natural starting point for inquiry, so this supports the department's 2027 inquiry work directly.
items.try: CL and TL: write one essential question for the units chosen for STAR above.

items.name: Named thinking routines
items.line: Think-Pair-Share and See-Think-Wonder are written into the lesson steps.
items.what: ML lesson plans name the routine to use at each step, and the same routines recur, so students come to know them.
items.where: Think-Pair-Share appears in all 32 ML guide and SOW files. Other thinking routines are named in 27.
items.gap: TL names routines in 25 of its 97 lesson files, such as KWL, Think-Pair-Share, Connect-Extend-Challenge and What Makes You Say That, but no set recurs across courses. CL uses thinking maps (思维图) but does not name these routines. They stay in the guides: SLS lessons do not use them.
items.why: Students taking two languages could meet the same routines in both, which reduces how much has to be taught twice.
items.try: All three: agree two or three shared routines for Sec 1.

items.name: Say it, write it, check it
items.line: Oral rehearsal before writing, then a peer check against a checklist.
items.what: Students talk through their ideas using word and sentence scaffolds, write, then read to a partner and check against a checklist. In G1 the same routine runs for four years, and only the scaffolds thin out.
items.where: The CL G1 teacher guides, through the writing blocks of each unit, supported by SLS writing packages. G2, G3 and Higher use planning, writing and revising with checklists.
items.gap: ML discusses a model text and then writes, with no fixed check step. TL has self or peer assessment in 43 of its 97 lesson files, without a set routine.
items.why: It supports weaker writers, and all three languages share the same SEC paper structure.
items.try: ML: the response-text tasks in Sec 3. TL: one production task in Sec 1.

TL.t: Self or peer check in 43 of 97 files

items.name: Differentiation advice in each guide
items.line: Suggestions for adjusting a lesson up or down for different learners.
items.what: CL guides include a section of differentiation suggestions (差异性处理) for teaching points, not only general advice.
items.where: All 60 CL guide files.
items.gap: ML guides offer some enrichment (Pengayaan) and scaffolding notes, about 30 mentions in all. TL's Word overviews do not have it. Three of TL's 97 lesson files name it: G1 1A (sheets for average and high-ability students), G1 2A (grouping by attainment) and G3 1B Unit 3 (mixed pairs). SLS gives no advice either, though read-aloud comes in separate versions by course.
items.why: Every language teaches a range of learners, and teachers should not have to work out the adjustments alone each time.
items.try: ML: add support and stretch notes to one G2 unit. TL: do the same for one G1 unit.

items.name: One named reading skill per unit
items.line: Each unit teaches one reading skill by name, tied to the theme.
items.what: Each CL unit names the reading skill it teaches and anchors it in the text, so the skills build across the year.
items.where: The CL teacher guides, in each unit's learning-content table and reading block.
items.gap: ML reading sits inside each part with no skill named per unit, apart from the Sec 4 Unit 5 critical-reading toolkit. TL names no skill per unit, but 29 of its 97 lesson files name a reading strategy. Directed Reading Thinking Activity, in 15 of them, is in no CL or ML file under that name.
items.why: Students and teachers can see which reading skill they are building, and every language is examined on reading comprehension.
items.try: ML: bring the Sec 4 Unit 5 toolkit forward into a Sec 3 unit. TL: name one skill per unit in Sec 3.

TL.t: Strategies in 29 of 97 files, not per unit

items.name: ASiBiDiBaM answer frame for online posts
items.line: One frame for every G1 online post: greeting, the six question words with feelings, then a closing.
items.what: ML G1 teaches one answer frame from Sec 1 to Sec 4: greet the writer, answer with ASiBiDiBaM (Apa, Siapa, Bila, Di mana, Bagaimana, Mengapa: what, who, when, where, how, why) plus Perasaan (feelings), then close. By Sec 4 it adds 4P: Pengalaman, Perasaan, Pendapat, Pengajaran (experience, feelings, opinion, lesson).
items.where: Not in the CPDD guides. It is in the 2026 BVSS ML G1 papers and marking schemes (Sec 1 to 3 WA and EOY, Sec 4 NT), where 5 of the 10 marks are for organisation.
items.gap: CL G1 marking rewards answering each question in the post with reasons, but names no frame. The TL Sec 1 answer key lists when, where, activity and feelings, close to the same idea.
items.why: Weaker writers in G1 lose marks for missing points. A fixed frame they can recite gives every post the same shape.
items.try: CL and TL G1 2027 exam preparation booklets: write the frame in the language on the Part A skill card, then use it in every post chapter.

CL.t: No named frame in G1 posts

TL.t: Sec 1 answer key: when, where, activity, feelings

items.name: A Sec 1 to 4 ladder for G1 online posts
items.line: Sec 1 feelings, Sec 2 routines and home and school life, Sec 3 and 4 answers in the context of the question.
items.what: TL G1 stages the online post by level. Sec 1: how I feel, with sentence structure and feeling words. Sec 2: routines, home life and school life. Sec 3 and 4: answers built from the context of the question. The 2026 posts follow it: Tamil Language Festival and National Day (Sec 1), first day of school (Sec 2), Friendship Day (Sec 3).
items.where: Not in the CPDD guides. It is the TL team's practice, seen in the 2026 BVSS TL G1 papers and answer keys.
items.gap: CL G1 posts change topic from paper to paper (Teachers' Day, a zoo visit, family, sports day, community events), with no staged content or language. ML has the answer frame but does not stage topics by level.
items.why: Each year builds the language the next year needs, so Sec 4 students meet the exam's open questions already able to write feelings, routines and detail.
items.try: The 2027 G1 exam preparation booklets in all three languages now use this ladder as their Part A chapters (HOD, 16 Nov 2026).

items.name: GSCE sprint card for the Higher planned presentation
items.line: Generate, Sort, Connect, Elaborate: from video key words to three PEEL sub-points in 10 minutes.
items.what: HCL Sec 3 and 4 students plan the 2-minute presentation with Harvard Project Zero's Generate-Sort-Connect-Elaborate routine (列举、分类、链接、阐述) on one A4 sheet: topic and stand in the centre, key words from the narration, interviews and visuals in the inner ring while watching, sub-points 1 to 3 in the outer ring, then each sub-point spoken as Point, Evidence, Explain, Link. Worked mind maps on past topics and an opening template come with it.
items.where: Not in the CPDD guides. It is BVSS teachers' own material on the 2026 drive (HCL S3 and S4 GSCE口试冲刺卡, teacher and student versions).
items.gap: Higher ML (K356) and Higher TL (K357) have the same 2027 format, a planned presentation of up to 2 minutes from a video, then discussion. No named planning routine was found in ML or TL files, and the 2026 Sec 3 Higher Tamil mock oral still used the older reading-aloud format.
items.why: Ten minutes is short. A fixed routine turns watching into notes and notes into three supported points every time.
items.try: ML and TL Higher oral booklets 2027: redo the sprint card in Malay and Tamil, keeping the routine's name and credit.

ML.t: No planning routine found for HML

TL.t: No planning routine found for HTL

items.basis: Generate-Sort-Connect-Elaborate is a published Harvard Project Zero thinking routine from its Visible Thinking work (Ritchhart, Church and Morrison, 2011). Using it to plan the oral presentation is BVSS's own adaptation.

links.t: SCCL: Applying Thinking Strategies to Enhance Higher CL Oral Teaching (OPAL course CLI-000275)

items.name: Peer-assessment cards for the oral discussion
items.line: Pairs play examiner and candidate, then tick each step of the answer.
items.what: HCL students practise the discussion in pairs with examiner questions on a past topic. Lower-order questions: define the term, link to the video, give a life example, link back. Higher-order questions: two reasons, each with an example, which the card says is needed for the top band. Each step is marked done, incomplete or missing.
items.where: Not in the CPDD guides. It is BVSS teachers' own material on the 2026 drive (HCL S4 高华口试讨论 - 互评练习卡).
items.gap: No peer-practice card was found for ML or TL orals, or for the CL G1 to G3 conversation.
items.why: Students get many more speaking turns than with the teacher alone, and learn the marking by applying it.
items.try: All oral booklets 2027: one card per question type in the Part C toolkit.
items.basis: Peer assessment has a strong research base: a 2020 meta-analysis of 54 studies found it improves performance at every school level. Evidence for speaking alone is thinner, so treat the cards as promising rather than proven.

links.t: Double, McGrane and Hopfenbeck (2020): peer assessment meta-analysis, Educational Psychology Review

items.name: 4P planning sheet for the oral conversation
items.line: Experience, feelings, opinion, lesson on one sheet, with word banks for feelings and values.
items.what: ML Sec 4 students fill one sheet in the 10-minute preparation: Pengalaman (experience) with ASiBiDiBaM; Perasaan (feelings) and the setting, with feelings before and after for top marks; Pendapat (opinion) from four levels, self, school, community and nation, each with benefits and harms, developed with IJCK (Isi, Jelaskan, Contoh, Kaitkan: point, explain, example, link); Pengajaran (lesson: the values shown). Positive and negative feeling words, a values list and sentence starters sit on the same sheet.
items.where: Not in the CPDD guides. It is BVSS teachers' own material on the 2026 drive (ML M4n5 2026 4ML1ML2 Lisan Perbualan Templat).
items.gap: CL and TL frames stop at feelings and opinion. Neither has the lesson (values) step or a values word bank on one planning sheet.
items.why: One sheet matches the order the examiner asks in and makes the preparation time productive.
items.try: CL and TL oral booklets 2027: a planning sheet in the language with the four steps.

CL.t: Frames per question, no single sheet

TL.t: Frames per question, no single sheet

items.basis: 4P is common in Singapore ML schools, but each school's four Ps differ and MOE gives no definition (MLCS seminar papers). Its order follows Gibbs' reflective cycle (1988): description, feelings, evaluation, conclusion. Naming that parallel gives CL and TL a tried and tested frame to borrow.

links.t: University of Edinburgh: Gibbs' Reflective Cycle
MLCS professional learning (seminar papers and courses on Interaksi Lisan)
OPAL2.0: search 'Interaksi Lisan Dinamik' (ML oral interaction course)

items.name: Example ladder: cause, events, result
items.line: The same video example told in one line, in a few sentences, then in vivid detail.
items.what: CL teaches Q1 examples with a three-star ladder built on 起因、经过、结果 (cause, what happened, result), the structure the CPDD CL guides teach for telling an event: one sentence, then the sequence of events, then a second event and its result with detail. Students first spot whether the video shows one example, two big ones or many small ones to sum up, and learn to describe a word they do not know.
items.where: Not in the CPDD guides. It is BVSS teachers' own material on the 2026 drive (CL G2 S1 口语训练 举例与感受; BVSS 中一口语教学 and 举例与感受 slides).
items.gap: ML uses 5W1H (ASiBiDiBaM) for what to include but has no graded model of how much to say. No TL ladder was found, though the TL guides teach தொடக்கம், நிகழ்வு, முடிவு (beginning, event, ending) for stories.
items.why: Students hear exactly what a fuller answer sounds like, which a rubric line alone does not show.
items.try: ML and TL oral booklets 2027: one ladder per Q1 chapter with a BVSS video, each told in the language's own CPDD words.

ML.t: What to include, no graded model

items.basis: Each language already has CPDD words for telling an event: CL 起因、经过、结果 (cause, what happened, result), ML 5W1H with urutan peristiwa (sequence of events), TL தொடக்கம், நிகழ்வு, முடிவு (beginning, event, ending). All three match the classic narrative structure of Labov and Waletzky (1967): orientation, complicating action, resolution, evaluation.

items.name: See-Think-Wonder with 5W1H while watching the video
items.line: Who, when, where, what while watching; then how and why to prepare the answers.
items.what: CL G3 Sec 1 and 2 oral booklets use See-Think-Wonder (a Harvard Project Zero routine) with 5W1H during the preparation time: who, when, where, what and the narration's key words, then how (feelings, effects, what to avoid or encourage) and why.
items.where: Not in the CPDD guides. It is BVSS teachers' own material on the 2026 drive (CL G3 中一G3口试训练_2025, 中二G3口试训练_2026).
items.gap: ML uses 5W1H (ASiBiDiBaM) for answering Q1 but not as a viewing routine. No TL viewing routine was found.
items.why: Students watch with a purpose, so the video gives them examples for all three questions.
items.try: ML and TL oral booklets 2027: the video chapter (Part B) uses the same routine in the language.
items.basis: See-Think-Wonder is a published Harvard Project Zero routine. 5W1H is the standard set of journalistic questions and the term the CPDD ML guides use. ASiBiDiBaM, the Malay form BVSS ML teachers use, was found online only in Malaysian sources, and for writing, so 5W1H is the safer shared name.

links.t: SCCL: Teaching and Learning Interaction Strategies via iMTL Portal (Sec 3 CL toolkit)

items.name: Problem-Solution-Benefit and a connectives bank
items.line: A three-part suggestion answer, an opinion frame and connectives sorted by what they do.
items.what: TL oral practice gives a suggestion frame, பிரச்சினை, தீர்வு, பலன் (problem, solution, benefit), and an opinion frame, நிலைப்பாடு, காரணம், அனுபவம் அல்லது சான்று, மீண்டும் நிலைப்பாடு (opinion, reason, experience or evidence, opinion restated). A connectives bank (இணைப்புச் சொற்கள்) groups words for sequence, example, cause and effect, contrast, addition and conclusion.
items.where: Not in the CPDD guides. It is BVSS teachers' own material on the 2026 drive (TL Oracy Skills வாய்மொழித்தேர்வுப் பயிற்சி).
items.gap: CL's suggestion frame (who and what, how, why) has no benefit step. ML has sentence starters but no connectives sorted by function.
items.why: Ending a suggestion with its benefit answers the 'why' the examiner usually asks next.
items.try: CL and ML oral booklets 2027, Q2 chapter and Part C toolkit.
items.basis: The opinion frame is the widely taught PREP pattern (point, reason, example, point), close to CL's OREO. Problem-Solution-Benefit follows the problem-solution pattern of persuasive speaking, as in Monroe's motivated sequence; the one experiment on Monroe found listeners judged it better organised, not more persuasive. No official Tamil source names either frame.

links.t: Organizing persuasive speeches: Monroe's motivated sequence (Kirkwood, open textbook)

items.name: Idea ladders: one move, three names
items.line: Ideas from me, family, school, community, nation and world, so suggestions never run dry.
items.what: All three languages teach students to find ideas at several levels. TL: நான், குடும்பம், பள்ளி, சமூகம், நாடு, உலகம் (me, family, school, community, nation, world), with a grid per topic. ML: Diri, Sekolah, Masyarakat, Negara (self, school, community, nation), each with benefits and harms. CL: PIGSS, Parent (家长), Individual (个人), Government (政府), School (学校), Social media (社交媒体), for suggestions.
items.where: Not in the CPDD guides. It is BVSS teachers' own material on the 2026 drive (TL oral practice deck; ML 4ML1ML2 template; CL 2026 口语训练 提出建议).
items.gap: The same move has three shapes and three names, so students taking two languages learn it twice.
items.why: One shared ladder, said in each language, is learnt once and used in both.
items.try: Agree one ladder shape for all three oral booklets 2027.
items.basis: Project Zero's Circle of Viewpoints routine does the same job: list the people a topic touches, then speak from each viewpoint. Naming it gives the three ladders one tried and tested routine to share.

items.name: Today's Speaker: a daily speaking turn
items.line: Lower secondary: one student speaks on a set topic each lesson, with a word bank.
items.what: TL lower secondary uses இன்றைய பேச்சாளர் (Today's Speaker): a list of topics such as healthy living and Tamil heritage, each with a word bank, for a short speaking turn at the start of lessons.
items.where: Not in the CPDD guides. It is BVSS teachers' own material on the 2026 drive (TL Oracy Skills, Lower Sec இன்றைய பேச்சாளர் தலைப்புகள்).
items.gap: No regular speaking routine was found in CL or ML lower secondary files; oral practice clusters before the exams.
items.why: Small, frequent turns build fluency, which is marked in every oral rubric.
items.try: CL and ML Sec 1 and 2 in 2027: a weekly speaker slot using the oral booklet topics.
items.basis: Regular low-stakes talk is a core idea of the oracy work by Voice 21 and Oracy Cambridge. No Singapore source names a Today's Speaker routine. MOE's PDTL site has a secondary Tamil spoken-interaction model, tested in four volumes of teachers' action research.

links.t: PDTL (MOE): Spoken Interaction for Secondary, பேச்சுவழிக் கருத்துப்பரிமாற்றம்

method: What counts as found: the term or practice appears in the guide text, searched on 4 Nov 2026 across every CL, ML and TL guide and syllabus on the department's drive. Counts are from that search and are approximate.

Limits: the TL lesson PDFs have a faulty font encoding. Their text was repaired offline and searched in Tamil and English on 5 Nov 2026. A text search finds what a guide names, so unnamed practice can be missed. A few words stay wrong and a few pages are images only.
Not found means not named in the guides. Teachers may well be doing this in class already.
The “First place to try” lines are department suggestions, not CPDD advice. They still need the language teams' judgement.

summaries.title: The clearest gap: E21CC (Emerging 21st Century Competencies)
summaries.intro: The 2021 CPDD guides say 21CC. MOE's 2023 milestones document and the BVSS 2027 focus areas say E21CC.
items: Its guides explain how to set a unit's 21CC goal and give four developmental levels, but work through only one unit.
Only five teacher notes in G1 Sec 4 Units 1 to 3 name a 21CC. ML is stronger on inquiry and thinking routines.

Its overviews tag 21CC activity by activity across the courses, but name the competency without a level or a way to set goals. The SLS lessons do not repeat the tags: 1 of the 282 on the hub's unit cards prints codes and levels.
summaries.note: Put together, CL's method and TL's map would give all three languages a shared way to plan the 2027 E21CC priorities.

summaries.title: Inquiry across the three languages: IBL (inquiry-based learning)
summaries.intro: IBL becomes a BVSS approach from 2027. The shared MTL syllabus does not name it as an approach, so each language got there differently.
items: Its syllabus names inquiry four times, and 57 of its 92 integrated tasks have students find out for themselves. No guide tags any of them as inquiry (department reading).
Its syllabus lists STAR, used in 4 G2 and G3 units. G1 and G2 Sec 3 Unit 4 are flagged as inquiry and usable as a WA, and units are built around essential questions.
TL has the theory and a few examples

Syllabus section 4.9 sets out inquiry. The guides tag it in G3 2A Units 2 and 3, use the 5E steps in G3 2B Units 1 and 2, and name it as the strategy in HTL Sec 3 Units 1 and 3. That is all a text search of the repaired lesson files found. None of the 282 SLS lessons on the hub's unit cards names inquiry or a method.
summaries.note: Put together, CL's tasks give the occasions, ML's STAR gives the steps and flags tasks for WA, and TL's 5E shows inquiry applied to reading.

tlsls.title: What the Tamil SLS lessons add
tlsls.intro: The department read Tamil SLS on 4 Nov 2026 to see what it adds to the guides: all 282 lessons on the hub's unit cards, the 125 other teaching and resource lessons, and a sample of each long series.
tlsls.finding: SLS is mostly a media shelf. In about three in four unit-card lessons, students answer nothing in SLS: the task is in the workbook or textbook. The teaching design, including inquiry and the 21CC tags, stays in the guides.
rows: The audio or video track, 6 to 22 minutes in the lessons checked. The 2020 batch has its questions in SLS; later ones leave them to the workbook.
The clip. The questions are in the workbook.
Mostly one opener video or interactive package. A few have open or voice tasks.
Clean, searchable Tamil passages with questions. Some have suggested answers.
The most developed series, edited June 2026: 20 marks, a rubric and SLS speech evaluation in Tamil, by course and level.
E-books as packages at lower levels; open or recorded questions in the later years.
Series the Word overviews do not name by these titles. Sampled, not read in full.
Full papers with passages and marks.
